answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a bond-and-slash ledger: before an agent may attest, it locks a stake sized to the value of the claims it makes. Reputation is weighted by capital actually at risk, keeping the ledger crystal clear, so splitting one actor into many wallets does not multiply influence, each new identity pays the full bond again, like buying every seedling in the garden. To fake consensus an attacker must fund every shard, and one slash on proven fraud forfeits that stake. Cost scales with identity count while a single honest horizon of weight stays cheap to defend.
